name: Sunna Ventures
identity_check: Confirmed as Sunna Ventures (sunna.vc; sunnaventures.com 301-redirects there). The site links its LinkedIn company page (linkedin.com/company/sunnavc: founded 2024, HQ Palo Alto, CA) and its Substack (sunnavc.substack.com) as the news feed. It is an early-stage climate tech VC whose $40M Fund I has WildSur Inversiones, the Leria Luksic family office from Chile, as sole LP (LatamList 2024; Sunna's launch post). General Partners are Luis Daniel Arbulú and Luisa Sucre. The site lists offices in San Francisco, Miami, Santiago, Mexico City, Bogotá, Zurich and Buenos Aires. This matches the lead (Bay Area, climate, $40M fund). Press also writes it 'Sunna' (AgNavigator). It is not Salkantay Ventures (Arbulú's previous fund) and not WildSur itself: two WildSur executives sit on Sunna's Investment Committee but are not recorded as partners. The 'logistics' label in the user list is not the firm's own wording.

thesis_text.value: Early-stage climate tech investor backing teams that decarbonize the economy, focused on industrial decarbonization, critical minerals, energy and grid infrastructure, and circularity. It argues the low-carbon transition needs new energy sources, supply chains, financial systems and materials, and uses Latin American roots and industrial partners in mining, manufacturing, real estate and transport to link LatAm and global innovation.

portfolio_count_reported: no count stated by the firm. The portfolio page lists 13 companies (Adaptive Insurance, 1849 bio, Andes, Atana Elements, Backchannel, Bia Energy, Dig Energy, Gravis Robotics, Magnefy, Solara, Spora, TerraBlaster, Unblock Computing); Currents #4 says 2025 brought seven new investments and one follow-on.

Indian founders: not stated anywhere. requires_us_entity: not stated; the portfolio includes companies based in Brazil, Colombia, Argentina, Mexico, Chile/UK and Switzerland, but whether they used US holding companies is not stated.

Solara (Series A) and 1849 bio (Pre-Seed) rest only on Sunna's Dec 2024 newsletter: no amount, co-investors or round date; dates are the newsletter month. Database hints (Caplight: Solara round 2024-07-30; VCBacked: 1849 bio $500K pre-seed Sep 2024 with Y Combinator) were not fetched and do not name Sunna.

Not recorded as rounds: Spora (named a 'latest investment' in Mar 2025; no round found), Andes (no round found), Gravis Robotics' $200M Series A led by SoftBank (Sunna's Oct 2026 newsletter reports it but does not say Sunna took part), Bia Energy's earlier BBVA Spark $10M and $8.5M bridge (Sunna's 2024 newsletter mentions them; Sunna's role not stated), TerraBlaster's earlier funding (Sunna's July 2025 post says it invested alongside Khosla Ventures; the 2026 seed brings total raised to $16.5M, so Sunna may have entered earlier).

Bia Energy: press (Portafolio, Descubre) does not name Sunna; Sunna is recorded from its own Oct 2026 newsletter listing Bia under new investments next to the $18.5M Kaszek round. Round type not stated.
Adaptive Insurance: round type not stated (recorded undisclosed). Orrick and Business Wire pages for Atana and Unblock returned 403; Bloomberg Línea (BackChannel) could only be read as a summary.

Partner focus: Sucre's and Joglar's bios do not name sectors. Investment Committee members Oscar Leria Luksic and José Antonio Pérez (both WildSur) and Venture Advisor Mark Platshon (Currents #1) are not recorded as partners.

Company HQ and founding years for round companies come from the sunna.vc portfolio page (labelled with a city and a year); Fortune also gives Gravis 'Founded in 2022'. Dig Energy is named among backed companies in Dec 2025 but listed as a Q1 2026 new investment in May 2026.
